over rising gas prices as renewed U.S. strikes against Iran pushed oil prices higher and intensified concerns about fuel costs for American families.
Trump Says Oil Prices Will Fall
On Wednesday, in a post on
X
, Schumer shared an Oval Office video clip showing Trump responding to questions about the renewed U.S. military campaign against Iran and its impact on oil prices.
A reporter told Trump that the strikes had pushed
a barrel. Trump responded that prices "will come down."
Asked how long the renewed campaign would last, Trump said, "I don’t think too long."
Trump also defended the U.S. position around the Strait of Hormuz, saying, "we’ve controlled and we are controlling the Hormuz Strait."
He added, "We are bringing lots of boats out every day with millions of barrels of oil."
Schumer Slams Trump Over Gas Prices
Schumer criticized Trump in his post, arguing that Americans have been waiting for relief from elevated fuel costs.
"For 6 months, Americans have been hearing this from Trump," he wrote.
He added, "Gas prices just hit the highest-ever for August, families are begging for relief, and this is the best Trump can do."
American Automobile Association data showed the national average for regular gasoline at $4.1203 a gallon Wednesday, compared with $3.1869 a year earlier.
The highest prices were in California at $5.7369 a gallon, followed by Washington at $5.4373 and Hawaii at $5.4157.
